notes: Run each case >=3x against Opus + Sonnet at minimum; baseline is `without_skill` (no SKILL.md, no reference.md, no react-native.md in context).

Without the skill, models tend to parse the webhook body before checking auth, use `===` instead of a timing-safe compare, and skip the requestId idempotency step — watch for those specifically in the baseline run.
`assertions` are necessary mechanically-checkable conditions, not exhaustive.
Cases 1-3 cover Vouch hosted verification (private data). Case 4 covers the Social Data API (public data) — watch for models reaching for getDataSourceUrl when no end user is involved.

evals.prompt: I'm adding Instagram creator verification with follower count to our payout flow. Generate the hosted verification URL and write the webhook handler that checks auth and persists the verified account.
evals.expected_output: Uses @getvouch/sdk's getDataSourceUrl with an Instagram datasourceId, redirectBackUrl, optional webhookUrl, and a metadata payload kept under 256 characters. The webhook handler reads the Authorization header and rejects with 401 using a timing-safe comparison against `PSK <secret>` BEFORE parsing the JSON body. Only after auth passes does it parse outputs/webProofs and persist the event keyed by requestId so retries are idempotent (e.g. unique constraint + catch 23505, or onConflict upsert).
assertions: Webhook handler checks the Authorization/PSK header and can return 401 before any call to parse/await the JSON body
Uses a constant-time comparison (e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual) for the secret check rather than plain `===` or `includes`
metadata passed to getDataSourceUrl is JSON.stringify'd and the response notes or respects the 256-character cap
Persistence step is idempotent by requestId (unique constraint + conflict handling, or an explicit dedupe check) rather than a plain insert with no duplicate handling
Does not treat outputs or webProofs as trustworthy before the auth check has passed

evals.prompt: Compliance wants us to independently verify the web proof cryptographically instead of just trusting whatever the webhook outputs say.
evals.expected_output: Submits each webProof's presentationJson to POST https://app.getvouch.io/api/v1/verify, checks that the response indicates success before treating the proof as valid, and accounts for webProofs being absent on sensitive datasources (so this step is conditional, not assumed to always run).
assertions: POSTs to https://app.getvouch.io/api/v1/verify with presentationJson in the request body
Checks a success/validity field on the response and rejects or throws when verification fails, rather than assuming any 2xx response means valid
Notes or handles the case where payload.webProofs is absent (e.g. guards with `?? []` or an explicit check) rather than assuming it's always populated

evals.prompt: We have a React Native app and want users to verify bank account ownership without leaving the app.
evals.expected_output: Recommends the @getvouch/react-native-sdk embedded flow (VouchSDK.initialize + VouchSDK.start) instead of the hosted getDataSourceUrl + redirect flow, notes that webhookUrl is required in start(), and guards the flow with an iOS version/support check before starting verification.
assertions: Recommends @getvouch/react-native-sdk / VouchSDK.start rather than getDataSourceUrl for this in-app use case
States that webhookUrl is a required field in VouchSDK.start params
References an iOS support/version guard (e.g. VouchSDK.isSupported()) before starting verification, or explicitly notes iOS 14-16.3 is unsupported

evals.prompt: A brand pasted an Instagram post URL into our campaign form. Pull the like and comment counts for that post and tell me who liked it, then retry sensibly when the scraper is rate limited.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Social Data API rather than the Vouch SDK, because this is public data with no end user to verify. Reads metrics via GET /admin/challenges/{challengeId}/metrics and checks lastRefresh, not just data.fetchedAt, before trusting the counts. Drives likers as an async job: POST .../likers/refresh, poll .../likers/status until a terminal status, then page .../likers. Retries only transient failures (429/502/503), honours Retry-After, and treats 404, 422, 401 and 403 as permanent.
assertions: Reaches for the Social Data API endpoints rather than @getvouch/sdk getDataSourceUrl for this public-data request
Treats likers as asynchronous: starts a refresh, polls a status endpoint, and only then reads rows, rather than expecting likers inline
Bounds the polling loop with a deadline or maximum attempt count instead of looping until a terminal status forever
Does not retry 401 or 403, and does not retry the permanent scraping codes (POST_NOT_FOUND, POST_NOT_ACCESSIBLE, POST_AGE_RESTRICTED)
Reads Retry-After for 429 rather than using a fixed sleep, and does not assume the header is always numeric seconds
Notes that likers are Instagram-only, or that fetched liker counts may undercount the visible like count
